content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I have a [product_name] and an HMI panel. I want to connect another HMI panel at a location about 100 meters away. Is it possible to do this using a LAN cable? Any advice would be appreciated. Thanks.
Hello [user_name], According to the manual, the maximum recommended length is 100 meters when using CAT5e cable. Please refer to the attached document.

Hello [user_name], What was mentioned earlier is correct, but you can increase the effective length by inserting a network switch between the devices. Typically, it's best to keep cable runs below 90 meters. If it's possible to install a switch between the [product_name] and the HMI panels, you should have reliable communication as HMIs generally do not create significant network traffic.

analysis.insight_summary: Participants are looking for advice on connecting two HMI panels over a 100-meter distance using a LAN cable alongside a [product_name]. Guidance includes the official maximum Ethernet cable length (100 meters with CAT5e) and practical recommendations such as using a switch to extend network range and uphold communication reliability. The discussion balances official specifications with real-world networking strategies for industrial setups.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect straightforward solutions and recommendations that enable dependable LAN connectivity between a [product_name] and two distant HMI panels. Suggestions for cabling standards and extending network reach for consistent performance are sought.
